subject: Cognitive Science
title: Joint Attention
description: A quick win: understand Joint Attention.

hook.text: A nine-month-old follows Mom's gaze to a dog, then looks back at Mom. She's sharing focus.

buildup.text: Joint attention is when two people focus on the same object by tracking gaze or pointing.

discovery.text: It appears around nine months and is the foundation for language, social learning, and culture.

twist.text: Delays in joint attention are among the earliest signs of autism—before other symptoms appear.

climax.text: Without it, word learning stalls: a child must know what a parent is looking at to learn a label.

quiz.question: Why is joint attention important for language learning?
options: Children need to know what a speaker is referring to
